title: A Summer for the Promise
premise: Ines Zhou's struggling café is saved from foreclosure only when she learns she has inherited half of a stubborn island orchard — and the other half belongs to Theo Marchetti, the man she loved and left ten years ago. Forced to co-manage the orchard through one last summer season, they clash over debts, a predatory developer, and the town's hunger for justice after the orchard's late owner was cheated out of his land decades ago. As the ferry's final autumn departure approaches, Ines and Theo must expose the old fraud, choose whether the orchard is a prison or a home, and finally say the sentence they have rehearsed for a decade. In the end they keep the orchard, save the café, and leave on the last ferry together — not apart.
about_author: Beatrix Joubert is a former pastry chef who traded early-morning ovens for late-night manuscripts, writing love stories set in small coastal towns where food is a language. She lives on an island reachable only by ferry and insists every romance deserves a deadline.

chapters.title: Three Missed Payments
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines bakes through the night to meet a bank deadline and fails; the café is ninety days from gone. Emotional beat: exhausted defiance masking fear.

chapters.title: A Letter in a Lawyer's Envelope
chapters.summary: Ines POV. A lawyer's letter announces an inheritance: half of Marchetti Orchard, willed by a great-uncle she barely knew. Emotional beat: bewildered, cautious hope.

chapters.title: The Other Name on the Deed
chapters.summary: Ines POV. At the reading, Ines learns the co-heir is Theo Marchetti — the man who broke her heart ten years ago. Emotional beat: the past slamming into the present.

chapters.title: The Ferry Arrives
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo steps off the ferry intending to sell his half and leave; he sees Ines on the dock. Emotional beat: dread and longing in equal measure.

chapters.title: Terms of Co-Existence
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The heirs meet with the lawyer and agree to a summer trial: run the orchard together or the land goes to auction. Emotional beat: brittle professionalism.

chapters.title: The Orchard in June
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo surveys the overgrown rows, the crumbling press house, and the old man's ledger full of debts. Emotional beat: grief for the uncle he abandoned.

chapters.title: Flour and Grudges
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines tests an orchard-fruit pastry for the café, refusing to admit the fruit tastes like memory. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness.

chapters.title: The Developer's Card
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A sleek developer, Corliss Vane, offers each heir a fortune to sell — separately, to divide them. Emotional beat: temptation with teeth.

chapters.title: First Harvest Meeting
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines organizes the pickers, discovering the crew are townsfolk the uncle quietly kept employed. Emotional beat: responsibility taking root.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Doesn't Say
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo finds gaps in his uncle's accounts — payments to someone unnamed, going back forty years. Emotional beat: suspicion kindled.

chapters.title: A Storm, One Roof
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A summer storm traps them in the press house; old wounds spill out — why Ines left, why Theo never followed. Emotional beat: the argument a decade overdue.

chapters.title: The Sentence She Rehearsed
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines almost says the rehearsed sentence — an apology and confession in one — and chokes. Emotional beat: terror of vulnerability.

chapters.title: Café on the Brink
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The bank issues a final notice; Ines realizes the orchard income could save the café if the harvest succeeds. Emotional beat: stakes braided together.

chapters.title: Vane's Second Offer
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Vane raises his offer and hints he knows something damaging about the deed's history. Emotional beat: unease beneath greed.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At a harvest supper, old-timers hint the uncle's land was swindled from a family named Okafor generations ago. Emotional beat: buried injustice surfacing.

chapters.title: Cherries at Midnight
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo and Ines pick by lantern-light to beat a heat wave, working in easy rhythm for the first time. Emotional beat: warmth neither will name.

chapters.title: The Okafor Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines tracks down Amara Okafor, a schoolteacher whose family lost the orchard to a forged sale. Emotional beat: guilt by inheritance.

chapters.title: Forged Signature
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Amara shows them the 1980s deed with a signature that isn't her grandfather's. Emotional beat: cold certainty of fraud.

chapters.title: Theo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo secretly considers selling to Vane to pay off the orchard's debts and free Ines from the café crisis. Emotional beat: love mistaken for sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Almost-Kiss
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. After a festival, wine, and an old song, they nearly cross the line — and Ines pulls back, terrified. Emotional beat: aching suspension.

chapters.title: Ledger Decoded
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines cracks the uncle's cipher: he was secretly paying the Okafors restitution for forty years — and Vane's firm bought the original forged deed. Emotional beat: righteous anger.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Auction Threat
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vane triggers a clause forcing auction unless both heirs file a fraud claim before the last ferry of the season. Emotional beat: the deadline becomes the story's clock.

chapters.title: Lawyers and Long Shots
chapters.summary: Theo POV. A weary local attorney says the fraud claim is winnable but needs the original ledger and a living witness. Emotional beat: fragile resolve.

chapters.title: The Witness in the Hills
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They find the uncle's former farmhand, now ninety, who saw the forgery happen — but he's failing fast. Emotional beat: racing against mortality.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The old man gives his deposition, naming Vane's predecessor; Ines realizes her great-uncle spent his life atoning. Emotional beat: sorrow transmuted to purpose.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Bank
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Theo's secret meeting with Vane is exposed; Ines believes he sold them out. Emotional beat: the old wound reopened, deeper.

chapters.title: The Empty Press House
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Ines works the harvest alone, furious and heartsick, while the café fails one payment from closure. Emotional beat: rock bottom.

chapters.title: What Theo Actually Signed
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Revealed: Theo signed a decoy contract to bait Vane into producing the forged deed as proof of title. Emotional beat: the trap snapping shut.

chapters.title: Vane's Counterstroke
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Vane, cornered, threatens to demolish the press house before the claim is heard. Emotional beat: desperation on both sides.

chapters.title: The Town Stands Up
chapters.summary: Ines POV. Pickers, café regulars, and the Okafors form a human chain at the press house; the sheriff, himself a debtor, declines to enforce. Emotional beat: justice outside the law.

chapters.title: The Rehearsed Sentence, Said
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. In the press house at night, Ines finally says the sentence — 'I left because I loved you too much to watch you shrink for me' — and Theo answers with his own decade-old confession. Emotional beat: the dam breaking.

chapters.title: The Hearing
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Before the county clerk, the fraud claim is argued; the forged deed is invalidated and the Okafor family restored a share. Emotional beat: hard-won, imperfect justice.

chapters.title: Vane Withdraws
chapters.summary: Theo POV. Exposed and outmaneuvered, Vane sells his claim cheaply to the town trust. Emotional beat: quiet triumph.

chapters.title: The Last Ferry of the Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The final ferry departs with neither of them on it; they stand on the dock, having chosen to stay. Emotional beat: the deadline transformed into a vow.

chapters.title: Harvest Day
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The full orchard is picked; the first press of the new cider is shared with the whole town. Emotional beat: abundance earned.

chapters.title: Café Reborn
chapters.summary: Ines POV. The café reopens with an orchard menu and Amara as partner; the debt is cleared. Emotional beat: survival redefined as community.

chapters.title: The Uncle's Last Letter
chapters.summary: Theo POV. A letter the uncle left with the lawyer is finally opened, blessing the heirs and asking forgiveness. Emotional beat: grief resolved into gratitude.

chapters.title: Planting Season
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. They plant new rows together, planning an orchard school with the Okafors. Emotional beat: future taking root.

chapters.title: First Frost
chapters.summary: Ines POV. First frost silvers the trees; Ines and Theo close the season side by side, at peace with the price they paid. Emotional beat: stillness after the storm.

chapters.title: A Summer for the Promise
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Epilogue one year on: the café and orchard thrive, the ferry returns in spring, and Ines says a new sentence — 'stay' — which Theo does. Emotional beat: promise kept, love in the present tense.
